about: Mitigati for two, «il giuoco di tutte le carte in due persone» of the Turin rulebook «Primi elementi e regole del giuoco de' tarocchi» (Torino, Soffietti, 1787, pp. 85-87), read on the scan: the whole pack is used; because 78 cards in the hand are «una confusa faragine» the dealer discards thirteen cards and his opponent twelve (honours never; read as exact, the other reading, up to thirteen, is in the source text), then the dealer deals again all the cards that remain, half each, keeping three more for the usual dealer's discard (pp. 85-86); honours and ten or more trumps are declared before the first trick is covered and paid in marche, Mitigati (Angel, Bagatto, Fool) separately (p. 86, tariff of pp. 93-95); the rest is as in Venticinque for two; the hand is won with 46 points, the Fool's card deducted, counted in pairs (p. 87); a revoke or a misdeal costs ten marche, «una ficcia» (p. 87). The size of the first deal is not printed; the file follows Dummett's reading (26 and 25); 39 and 39 cannot be, as no cards would be left for the second deal. Marks: [D] documented, [R] our reading, [S] sources silent.

torino1846.cite: L. B., Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, part I (Grammatica del giuocatore), Torino, Serra, [1846]

dummett1980.cite: M. Dummett, The Game of Tarot, London, Duckworth, 1980; chapter XIII, pp. 258-279 (partial scan held, p. 268 missing)

prammatica1846.cite: L. B., Prammatica del giuocatore di tarocchi ossia regole indispensabili per gli amatori di simile passatempo, Torino, Serra, [1846] (separate issue, cover dated 1846, deposited 27 December 1845; reprinted from the same setting, same pages, as part II of Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, Torino, Serra, [1846])

count.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 85: «Anche fra due persone usasi di giuocare con tutto il mazzo dei Tarocchi»: two players.

direction.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 35, 37: «gli altri sempre a destra procedendo»: play passes to the right; with two players the direction changes nothing.

first_dealer.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 16: cards are turned up for each side, «se viene prima da questa parte un Trionfo, mischierò io»: the side that first receives a trionfo shuffles and deals first.

cut_by.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 16-17: the player on the dealer's left cuts («di dar a coppare a chi ti siede a sinistra»); if he declines the next on the left, if all decline the dealer deals as the pack lies.

cut_min.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 16: «Una carta sola non si può coppare»: the page forbids only a cut of one card; that each part keeps at least two cards is our reading.

dealer_rotation.source: [S] Ours: the deal alternates; Torino 1787, pp. 85-87 do not say who deals next. [R] Torino 1787, p. 41 (said in Sedici): «rimetterai le carte tutte in mazzo al tuo compagno»: the winner hands the cards to his companion, who shuffles and deals; with two players the loser of a hand would deal the next one.

mode.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 85, 87: two persons, the one who makes forty-six points wins and the opponent pays him: each for himself.

deck.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 85: «con tutto il mazzo dei Tarocchi»: «settant'otto Tarocchi» (see also pp. 9-10).

trump_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 13: «l'Angelo, il quale è il XX., appresso noi prende il Mondo»: the trionfi rank by their printed numbers, with the Angel XX above the World XXI («l'usanza, che in questo caso fa legge»); the Fool stands outside the order.

suit_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 11-13: in swords and batons the larger number takes the smaller; in cups and coins «la carta di numero inferiore prende quella di numero superiore, eccetto le figure» (the ace takes the two up to the ten); the courts stand above every numeral. [R] The order among the courts, King, Queen, Knight, Jack, is read from their points 5, 4, 3, 2 (pp. 13-14) and from the list of p. 10.

card_points.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 13-14: «Ogni Re conta cinque punti. Ogni Donna conta quattro punti»: king 5, queen 4, knight 3, jack 2, the Angel 5, Bagatto 5, the Fool 5; the World and the other cards carry no value of their own. Values are the book's numbers (a king with a plain card is 5, p. 52).

honours.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 34, 85: «mai non si scartino Re, nè altri Onori, che vagliano cinque punti»; the honours are the five-point cards, the kings, the Angel XX, the Fool and Bagatto (p. 34, rule 38).

fool.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 54, 87: «Il rimanente è come al giuoco semplice di Venticinque carte»; there «Folle non vien preso mai da alcun Trionfo, o cartaccia, ma solamente si mostra».

fool_exchange.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 52, 54, 87: «sarà in obbligo di dare al compagno una cartaccia»; it applies here through «Il rimanente è come al giuoco semplice di Venticinque carte» (p. 87). Also Torino [1846], part I, p. 39 (said of Chiamare il Re): «che dassi in compenso del Folle».

fool_exchange_card.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 52: «qualunque gli piaccia»; it applies here through «Il rimanente è come ...» (p. 87).

fool_exchange_to.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 52, 54, 87: «darai a me la carta del Folle» (p. 54): the card goes to the opponent, as in Baronetti, to which p. 87 sends through Venticinque. With two players this is always the one who takes the trick. Torino [1846], part I, p. 33 (Venticinque for three) gives it to «chi ha presa o coperta la mano».

fool_last_trick.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 50, 54: the Fool is never taken, in the last trick as in every other.

fool_no_tricks.source: [S] Torino 1787, p. 50: «non sarò io obbligato a dartelo mai»; Prammatica [1846], p. 6 disagrees («cederlo»), not followed.

replace.what: the Fool of a player who won no trick: kept or given up

options.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 21 (rule 10): «quanto si giuochi la partita semplice, qualunque sia il giuoco, che facciasi»: the stake of the simple game is settled before the deal. The book names no amount (p. 15 plays «un quattrino per ciascuna partita» as an example); the list of choices is the table's.

[D] Torino 1787, p. 93: «siasi conchiuso di quanto vaglia la marca»: before the game the players settle what a marca is worth. The book names no value; the list of choices is the table's. On the pages of this game only the ficcia is printed in marche (p. 87); the declarations are in marche through the tariff of pp. 93-95 (p. 86: «come a pagina 98»); the Bagatto payments rest on Torino [1846], part I, p. 53, not checked here; the payment for the game is a stake. [S] Revision 10: the engine does not multiply them yet: the honours and the trumps are a table it cannot scale.

phases.source: [S] Torino 1787, p. 85 says nothing of the first deal; that there is one is seen from «di bel nuovo, chi ha dato, ritorna a dare» (pp. 85-86). How many each receives is not printed.

hand_size.source: [S] Torino 1787, p. 85 and Torino [1846], part I, p. 50 print no number; ours: Dummett 1980, pp. 262-263 (26/25, discards 13 and 12). 39 and 39 cannot be: with discards of 13 and 12 no cards are left for the second deal.

replace.what: the size of the first deal

dealer_extra.source: [S] Ours after Dummett 1980, pp. 262-263: the first deal gives the dealer 26, written in hand_size.

phases.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 85: «chi dà, ne scarta … di tredici, e … ricevette ne scarta dodici».

who.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 85: both players discard, the dealer and «chi le ricevette».

count.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 85: the dealer «sino al numero di tredici», the other «dodici»: «ognuno cioè secondo le sue convenienze».

count_mode.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 85: «ne scarta a suo talento sino al numero di tredici» could read as a maximum for the dealer, while «ne scarta dodici» reads as exactly twelve. Read as exact for both: after the first deal of 26 and 25 (hand_size) and these discards each holds 13; the pack keeps 27 cards, the second deal gives 12 and 15, and after the dealer's second discard of three both hold 25 for the play. A dealer who put away fewer than 13 would hold more than 25 cards and the tricks could not be played out. Other reading: up to the number named.

replace.what: the size of the first deal and of the first discard

discard_honours_barred.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 85: «mai non si scartino Re, nè altri Onori, che vagliano cinque punti»; no exception is named here (the two of p. 34 are left out).

counts_for.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 21 (rule 10, for every game) speaks of a player without tricks «avendo o il Folle, o lo scarto»: the discard stays his. Prammatica [1846], pp. 24-25 takes both discards from him («perde i punti dei due scarti»); not followed, see OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, question 1.

replace.what: the discard of a player who won no trick: kept or lost

phases.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 85-86: «di bel nuovo, chi ha dato, ritorna … rimaste, del mazzo, metà per uno».

hand_size.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 86: «metà per uno»: half of the cards that remain to each player.

dealer_extra.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 86: «riserbandosene novellamente tre di più del suo compagno»: the dealer keeps three more.

dead.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 85: the dealer deals «tutte le carte, che son rimaste»: nothing is left over.

from.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 85-86: «ritorna a dare tutte le carte, che son rimaste, del mazzo, metà per uno»: the cards not yet dealt; so also Torino [1846], part I, p. 50 and Dummett 1980, p. 263.

phases.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 86: the three cards are for «nuovo, ma solito, ed usato scarto, ch'egli per se debbe fare».

who.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 86: the discard is the dealer's («ch'egli per se debbe fare»).

count.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 86: the three cards he reserved «debbono servire per ... scarto»; the usual dealer's discard of Venticinque is three (p. 53).

announce.source: [R] Torino [1846], part I, p. 50: the honours are declared «appena che chi distribuisce le carte abbia detto: ho scartato»; Torino 1787, p. 95 (three players) the same. Which of the two discards the words close is not said: read as the dealer's last discard, before the declarations.

discard_honours_barred.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 85: «mai non si scartino Re, nè altri Onori, che vagliano cinque punti».

counts_for.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 21 (rule 10, for every game) speaks of a player without tricks «avendo o il Folle, o lo scarto»: the discard stays his. Prammatica [1846], pp. 24-25 takes both discards from him («perde i punti dei due scarti»); not followed, see OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, question 1.

replace.what: the discard of a player who won no trick: kept or lost

window.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 86 prints the window: «prima dee accusarli, che coperta siasi la prima mano, o prima base»; p. 85: the honours are declared «(date che siansi, e ricevute le carte tutte)». It is played as at Bagatt'ultimo (p. 95): one declaring turn for each player before the first card, in the order of play; the table cannot tell when a declaration made while the first trick is open is still in time. Other reading: until the first trick is complete.

replace.what: when the declarations of Mitigati for two close

kinds.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 86, 93-95: «ognuno conta gli Onori, che ha, e gli accusa»; ten or more trumps are declared and as many are paid as are declared («tanti, quanti tu ne accuserai»); Mitigati, the Angel, Bagatto and the Fool («Chi avrà Angelo, Bagatto, e Folle, accuserà Mitigati», p. 93), «sarà pagato a parte» (p. 86). The tariff is that of the three-player text, to which the references «come a pagina 98» point (p. 98 is the vocabulary; the tariff stands on pp. 93-95): honours 3 → 10, 4 → 15, 5 → 20 and five more for each (p. 94), trumps one marca each from ten (p. 95), Mitigati 10 (p. 94, paid on top of the 10 for its three honours). Readings of ours: the threshold of three honours is carried over from the three-player text, where it is printed in words (p. 93: «se ne avrà solamente due, non gli accuserà»); the trumps are announced, not laid out (the lay-out is p. 93, three players). Other reading: honours from one, resting only on «ognuno conta gli Onori, che ha» (p. 86). Second reading of the tariff: p. 86 «L'istesso sottintendasi degli Onori» may mean the honours are paid one marca each, like the trumps; the tariff of p. 94 is followed. [D] p. 93: «se ne avrà solamente due, non gli accuserà, tanto meno un solo»: three at least.

late.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 86, 95: p. 86 requires the declaration before the first trick is covered; the forfeit of a late one is printed in the three-player text (p. 95), carried over.

mode.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 85-86, 93, 95: declaring is an obligation («debbonsi accusare», p. 85) and a late player loses his right: the player declares. Other reading: the engine declares for him.

paid.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 86, 94: the tariff is that of the three-player text, paid «subito, e non sul fine della partita».

paid_by.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 86, 94: the opponent pays; with a single opponent «da ambi i compagni» (p. 94, each or both together) makes no difference.

first_leader.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 54, 87: «Il rimanente è come al giuoco semplice di Venticinque carte»; there «l'altro compagno comincia a giuocare»: the dealer's opponent leads.

next_leader.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 50: «Chi prende giuoca sempre il primiero»; it applies here through p. 87.

follow_suit.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 49, 87: the answer in the suit asked, «senza mai rinegare», as in Venticinque.

must_trump.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 49, 87: «se non ho carte della medesima sequenza prendo con Trionfi» (Baronetti, to which p. 87 sends through Venticinque). Also Torino [1846], part I, p. 36, «anche negli altri giuochi»: «si risponderà e prenderà con un Trionfo». Torino 1787, p. 49 (Baronetti) prints the same duty: «se non ho carte della medesima sequenza prendo con Trionfi».

must_overtrump.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 49: the book states no duty to beat a trump on the table.

group.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 87: «le carte contansi a due a due».

count_unit.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 52, 87: the pair count of Baronetti; a card is worth its points less a half (a king with a plain card is 5).

odd_card.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 54-55, 87: «Una carta sola, ancorchè scompagnata» counts in Venticinque, to which p. 87 sends. Other reading: the odd card is dropped.

fool_card.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 87: «quarantasei punti, dedotta la carta del Folle»: the 46 are counted after the compensation card is given. Also Torino [1846], part I, p. 39 (said of Chiamare il Re).

trick_multipliers.source: [R] Torino 1787: the count is the one the section names; the book prints no trick multiplier and no war in these games (x2 and x4 are Duello's own).

last_trick_bonus.source: [R] Torino 1787: the book prints no bonus for the last trick (the +5 is Duello's own).

winner.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 87: «per guadagnare la partita di Mitigati in due persone, debbonsi fare quarantasei punti».

target.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 87: «quarantasei punti, dedotta la carta del Folle».

game_points.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 85-87: the hand is paid in marche and stake; the book names no game points.

tie.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 87: «Il rimanente è come al giuoco semplice di Venticinque carte»; 45½ each is not named, read as Venticinque, p. 54: «faremo eguali».

unit.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 86-87, 93: the declarations are paid in marche and the ficcia is ten marche; «siasi conchiuso di quanto vaglia la marca».

mode.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 87: with two players the loser pays «la partita»; the sum is not printed.

amount.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 85-87 name no payment of their own for Mitigati for two; ours: the simple game of p. 21 («quanto si giuochi la partita semplice»). Other reading [R]: Dummett 1980, p. 263 (a probable interpretation).

payments.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 85-87 are silent on the Bagatto; ours after Torino [1846], part I, p. 51: «vedi quanto ho detto parlando dell'altro Mitigati e del Bagatto dichiarato ultimo»; amounts p. 53. There only a declared Bagatto is paid (p. 51: «dichiara quindi Bagatto, se vuole»; p. 53: «quando l'abbia per tale dichiarato»); the engine plays no declaration, so the premium is paid without one. Other readings: no premium, as the book of 1787 is silent; or only a declared Bagatto, as Torino [1846]. See OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, question 17.

[S] Torino 1787, pp. 85-87 are silent on the Bagatto; ours after Torino [1846], part I, p. 51: «vedi quanto ho detto parlando dell'altro Mitigati e del Bagatto dichiarato ultimo»; amounts p. 53. There only a declared Bagatto is paid (p. 51: «dichiara quindi Bagatto, se vuole»; p. 53: «quando l'abbia per tale dichiarato»); the engine plays no declaration, so the premium is paid without one. Other readings: no premium, as the book of 1787 is silent; or only a declared Bagatto, as Torino [1846]. See OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, question 17.

[S] Torino 1787, pp. 85-87 are silent on the Bagatto; ours after Torino [1846], part I, p. 51: «vedi quanto ho detto parlando dell'altro Mitigati e del Bagatto dichiarato ultimo»; amounts p. 53. There only a declared Bagatto is paid (p. 51: «dichiara quindi Bagatto, se vuole»; p. 53: «quando l'abbia per tale dichiarato»); the engine plays no declaration, so the premium is paid without one. Other readings: no premium, as the book of 1787 is silent; or only a declared Bagatto, as Torino [1846]. See OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, question 17.

kind.source: [S] Ours: the book describes one hand and its marche; they are settled after every hand, the match ends after one round of dealers (match.dealer_rounds); the greatest balance wins, equal balances are a draw («pace»).

dealer_rounds.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 85-87 are silent on the length of a match: the book describes one hand and its payment. Ours: one round of dealers, two hands, each player dealing once; the payments are made after every hand and the greatest balance wins. A thrown-in hand (everybody passed, or a hand that is dealt again after equal points) counts as a dealt hand: nobody pays, the next player deals and the round goes on. The table may agree on two or three rounds.

effect.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 87: «Chi finalmente rinega, o … compagno dieci marche, … comunemente dicesi una ficcia». Torino 1787, p. 99: «Ficcia l'istesso, che marca», its worth as agreed. The book says «al compagno»: the opponent. Torino [1846], part I, p. 57: «Ficcia, lo stesso che marca», «e si fa valere più o meno, secondo si è convenuto»: there a ficcia is one marca of agreed worth.
[D] Torino 1787, p. 87: «dà giuoco fallo» (a card more or fewer than due, p. 18) costs the same ten marche, «una ficcia».

left_out.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 34 (rule 38): the Bagatto may be put away when it stands alone, without the Fool.
left_out.why: The engine bars the honours from the discard without this exception in this game.

left_out.source: [D] Dummett 1980, p. 263 (his guess, not PE): the winner receives 10 game points, or 20 if the loser has less than 23 card points, plus the amount by which he exceeds 46.
left_out.why: A reconstruction by Dummett, not a source; not written.
